accepted_recoveries: Scale the benchmark-owned stale canary to zero and preserve its manifest for rollback.
Increase the namespace CPU quota by the minimum required amount when cluster capacity and policy permit it.
forbidden_actions: Do not delete or scale down unrelated tenant workloads.
Do not remove the ResourceQuota object.
Do not reduce checkout resource requests below measured safe requirements merely to pass admission.
incident.injected_fault: A benchmark-owned stale canary reserves the remaining namespace CPU request quota, so new checkout replicas are rejected even though cluster nodes have capacity.
observable_signals: Checkout ReplicaSet events report exceeded quota for requests.cpu.
ResourceQuota status shows requested CPU at its hard limit.
Nodes retain enough allocatable CPU for the rejected replicas.
preconditions: The stale canary is labeled as benchmark-owned and has zero live traffic.
Worker nodes have capacity for the intended checkout replicas.
No LimitRange or scheduler constraint independently blocks the rollout.
required_evidence: Capture ResourceQuota hard and used values.
Attribute namespace CPU requests to their owning workloads.
Show that the stale canary is benchmark-owned and receives no traffic before reclaiming its quota.
incident.title: ResourceQuota saturation

constraints: Do not delete or scale down unrelated tenant workloads.
Do not remove the ResourceQuota object.
Do not reduce checkout resource requests below measured safe requirements merely to pass admission.

hypotheses.cause: Namespace ResourceQuota 'case-06-cpu-budget' requests.cpu limit (500m) is saturated because benchmark-owned deployment 'stale-canary' holds 300m of CPU requests while receiving zero live traffic, causing admission rejection of the 3rd 'checkout-api' replica (which requests 100m CPU).
supports: Deployment 'checkout-api' condition FailedCreate records: 'pods \"checkout-api-79bfd74cdd-l9cs7\" is forbidden: exceeded quota: case-06-cpu-budget, requested: requests.cpu=100m, used: requests.cpu=500m, limited: requests.cpu=500m'.
ResourceQuota 'case-06-cpu-budget' status shows used requests.cpu at 500m against a hard limit of 500m.
Pod 'stale-canary-7cc7bbbff5-wsnvp' requests 300m CPU and is labeled 'proofix.io/benchmark-owned: true' and 'proofix.io/live-traffic: false'.
The two existing 'checkout-api' pods request 100m CPU each (200m total), leaving 0m allocatable quota out of 500m.

hypotheses.cause: Cluster node capacity exhaustion on node 'vm-4' is preventing the default scheduler from binding new 'checkout-api' pods.
contradicts: Node 'vm-4' status reports 4 allocatable CPU cores with negligible overall CPU request allocation across running pods.
The 3rd replica failure occurs at ReplicaSet admission (FailedCreate) via ResourceQuota admission controller, before pod creation and scheduler evaluation.

hypotheses.cause: Workload container configuration or readiness probe failure is preventing 'checkout-api' replicas from achieving ready status.
contradicts: Both existing 'checkout-api' pods (d5svt and hnvmj) are currently Ready (status.phase Running, Ready=True) and active in Service Endpoints.
The unavailable replica count is due to a missing 3rd pod blocked at admission, not a failing running container.
supports: Historical event logs show transient readiness probe connection refused events during initial container boot.

payload.rationale: The ResourceQuota 'case-06-cpu-budget' in namespace 'proofix-case-06' has a hard limit of 500m requests.cpu which is saturated. The benchmark-owned deployment 'stale-canary' holds 300m CPU requests across 1 replica while receiving no live traffic. The deployment 'checkout-api' has 2 running replicas (100m CPU request each) and its 3rd replica is rejected at admission due to quota exhaustion. Scaling 'stale-canary' to 0 replicas frees 300m CPU requests, allowing 'checkout-api' to admit and run its 3rd replica.
payload.rollback_trigger: Rollback if scaling stale-canary to 0 fails to relieve the quota bottleneck, if checkout-api replicas do not reach ready status, or if SLO latency and error rate metrics degrade.

success_criteria.description: Deployment checkout-api scales to 3 ready replicas without FailedCreate admission errors, ResourceQuota used requests.cpu stabilizes at 300m/500m, and SLO targets (http_5xx_rate < 0.001, p95_latency_ms < 200) are met.
